# Draft:Tricoci University of Beauty Culture

----
}}
Tricoci University of Beauty Culture (TUBC) is a for-profit vocational institution providing post-secondary education in cosmetology, esthetics, barbering, nail technology, and instructor training. Founded in 2004, the school operates campuses across Illinois, Indiana, and Wisconsin. It is accredited by the National Accrediting Commission of Career Arts & Sciences (NACCAS) and is recognized by the United States Department of Education as eligible for federal financial aid.
History
Founding
Tricoci University of Beauty Culture was founded in 2004 by Mario Tricoci, an Italian-born beauty industry entrepreneur who began his American hairstyling career in Chicago in 1960. In 1963, Tricoci opened his first salon in Villa Park, Illinois, and later relocated to a larger location in Des Plaines, Illinois. In 1977, he opened what is described as the first domestically privately-owned salon inside a major shopping mall. In 1986, the Mario Tricoci Hair Salon & Day Spa in Arlington Heights, Illinois became the first day spa in the Midwest.
Prior to founding the university, Mario Tricoci operated a chain of upscale salons and day spas under the brands "Mario Tricoci Hair Salon & Day Spa" and "Mario Tricoci, Too," which later merged with Elizabeth Arden Red Door Salons & Spas. Following this transition, Tricoci launched the university as a way to give back to the beauty industry and to establish a new model of vocational beauty education focused on producing salon-ready professionals with advanced technical skills, professional ethics, and leadership values.
In 2024, the university celebrated its 20th anniversary, noting it had educated more than 15,000 graduates across its campuses since opening.
Growth and expansion
Since its founding at a single campus in Chicago's Northwest Side, Tricoci University expanded steadily into a multi-state institution. By 2021, the university had grown to 15 campuses across Illinois, Indiana, and Wisconsin.
In 2021, the university announced a new executive leadership team led by CEO Nate Swanson, whose background included Chief Operating Officer roles at CareerStep and American Intercontinental University. The new team launched initiatives including curriculum updates to embrace distance education, expanded student and career services, and an expansion of the Bridgeview, Illinois campus to accommodate growing student demand.
Academics
Programs
Tricoci University offers training programs in the following disciplines:
* Cosmetology – A 1,500-hour program covering hair cutting, coloring, styling, makeup artistry, and nail services. Full-time students typically complete the program in approximately 12 months; part-time students in approximately 20 months.
* Esthetics – A 750-hour program focused on skin care, facials, waxing, body treatments, and advanced makeup application. Full-time students can complete the program in approximately 20 weeks; part-time students in approximately 34 weeks.
* Barbering – A 1,500-hour program covering hair cutting, shaving, grooming, and styling.
* Nail Technology/Manicuring – Training in nail care, nail enhancements, and salon services. Available at select campuses.
* Instructor Training – A post-licensure program for licensed beauty professionals seeking to enter the field of education. Available at select campuses.
New student cohorts begin every six weeks at most campuses, allowing for rolling enrollment throughout the year rather than a traditional semester schedule.
Admissions
Tricoci University maintains an open admissions policy with a 100% acceptance rate. Applicants in Illinois must be at least 16 years of age by the first day of class; applicants in Indiana and Wisconsin must be at least 18 years of age by the time the program is completed in order to qualify for state licensing examinations. All applicants must hold a high school diploma, official high school transcripts, or a GED certificate. Instructor training applicants must additionally hold a current state license as a cosmetologist, esthetician, or nail technician.
Accreditation and financial aid
Tricoci University is accredited by the National Accrediting Commission of Career Arts & Sciences (NACCAS), an agency recognized by the United States Department of Education. NACCAS accreditation enables students to qualify for federal financial aid through FAFSA, including grants and loans. The university also offers institutional scholarships and interest-free monthly payment plans. The average annual cost of attendance after financial aid is approximately $13,105.
Campuses
Tricoci University operates campuses across three states.
Illinois
* Bridgeview (southwest Chicago suburbs) – Cosmetology, Esthetics, Barbering
* Chicago NE – Rogers Park – Cosmetology, Esthetics
* Chicago NW – Norwood Park (near O'Hare) – Cosmetology, Esthetics, Barbering, Instructor Training
* Elgin – Cosmetology, Esthetics
* Glendale Heights – Cosmetology, Esthetics
* Libertyville – Cosmetology, Esthetics
* Normal – Cosmetology, Esthetics
* Peoria – Cosmetology, Esthetics, Instructor Training
* Rockford – Cosmetology, Esthetics, Barbering, Instructor Training
* Urbana – Cosmetology, Esthetics
Indiana
* Bloomington – Cosmetology, Esthetics
* Highland – Cosmetology, Esthetics, Barbering, Instructor Training
* Indianapolis NE (Fishers) – Cosmetology, Esthetics, Barbering, Nail Technology, Instructor Training
* Lafayette – Cosmetology, Esthetics, Nail Technology
Wisconsin
* Janesville – Cosmetology
Recognition and awards
Chicago Tribune Top Workplaces
In 2025, Tricoci University of Beauty Culture was ranked #30 among small businesses (75–249 employees) on the Chicago Tribune's annual Top Workplaces list, administered by Energage. This was the first time the university appeared on the list, and it was described by a university spokesperson as the first beauty school ever to receive the honor. Rankings are determined exclusively by employee feedback and evaluate factors including organizational leadership, workplace culture, and work-life balance.
AACS Golden School Awards
The American Association of Cosmetology Schools (AACS) recognized Tricoci University with its most prestigious honor — the Golden School of the Year award — in two consecutive years.
In 2022, the Chicago Northwest campus was named AACS Golden School of the Year in the category of schools with more than 100 students. AACS executive director Cecil Kidd stated that the university "represents the best of the cosmetology schools in America."
In 2023, the Bridgeview campus was named AACS Golden School of the Year and also received the award for Best Facility. Additionally, the Bloomington, Indiana campus received the Golden School award for Best Placement, with a placement rate of 82.81% and a graduation rate of 87.67%.
